name: HyperFrames
tagline: A video factory for your AI agent: write what you see in code, and it hands you a finished movie
sentence: Give it a web page with animations and it records a pixel-perfect MP4 - so an AI coding agent can make a product demo, a tutorial or an ad without opening a video editor.

board.say: Your AI agent can write code and build websites, but it cannot make a video.
board.eg: To get a product demo, someone still has to open a screen recorder or an editor like Premiere.

board.say: You give it an HTML page with animations - the same code your agent already writes.
board.eg: An HTML page with a GSAP animation showing a dashboard filling in, or a Lottie icon spinning.

board.say: It opens the page in a hidden browser, plays every animation frame by frame, and records each one.
board.eg: Headless Chrome renders each frame, FFmpeg stitches them into a video at the frame rate you set.

board.say: You get a finished MP4 that looks exactly like the page, with smooth animations at any resolution.
board.eg: A 1080p demo video of your product, made from code, with no manual editing.

before: Making a product video means opening screen-recording software or hiring an editor.
AI coding agents can build apps and websites, but they stop at "here's a screenshot".
Automated video tools often stutter or miss animations because they capture in real time.
after: Your AI agent writes an HTML page, runs one command, and gets a finished MP4 back.
Frame-by-frame capture means **every animation plays perfectly**, even complex ones with GSAP or Three.js.
The same page renders at any resolution - 1080p, 4K, vertical for phone - without re-editing.
uses_note: It is about 6 months old. Mostly used by developers and AI agent builders so far, but several creators have published tutorial videos made with it.

uses.what: Created an entire video using Claude Code and HyperFrames to produce graphics for video content.
uses.result: Published the video and shared the workflow on X, calling it a new way to make videos from code.

uses.what: Made multiple video types - an 8-second explainer, a 30-second product investigation, a branded launch video, and a talking-head-to-motion-graphics transformation.
uses.result: Called it "a video team you speak to" and published a tutorial on her blog.

steps: Run `npx hyperframes init my-video` to scaffold a starter project.
Run `npx hyperframes preview` inside the folder to see a live preview with hot reload.
Run `npx hyperframes render` to produce a finished MP4 from your HTML.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes

If that scan passes: run `npx hyperframes init my-video`, then `cd my-video && npx hyperframes preview` to see the live preview, then `npx hyperframes render` to produce the MP4. 10 minutes max.

best_for: You build AI agents or tools that need to produce video output automatically
You want pixel-perfect recordings of web animations without screen capture
skip_if: You want to edit videos by hand - this is for automated, code-driven production
You need talking-head or camera-based video, not animated web content
You are not a developer: there is no visual interface

alternatives.name: Remotion
alternatives.line: React-based video creation: write React components and render them to video. More mature but React-only, and freemium (free for teams of 3 or fewer).

alternatives.name: Revideo
alternatives.line: MIT-licensed library for batch video generation from code. Community fork of Motion Canvas.

watch: **Developer-only tool.** There is no visual interface: you write HTML and run a command. This is for developers and AI agents, not for someone who wants to drag and drop.
**Pre-1.0 with rapid churn.** 400+ releases in 5 months, currently v0.8.80. The API may change, and users report the AI gets you about 80% of the way - human polish is still needed.
**Made by HeyGen.** HeyGen is a well-funded video AI company. HyperFrames is open-source (Apache 2.0), but HeyGen's core product is paid and cloud rendering ties into their platform.

sources.title: Sabrina Ramonov: HyperFrames makes unlimited free videos
